@graph.description: Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) is a tart North American berry whose A-type proanthocyanidins are thought to reduce the ability of E. coli bacteria to adhere to the urinary-tract lining. Its main studied use is preventing urinary tract infections: a large Cochrane systematic review concluded that cranberry products reduce the risk of repeat UTIs in some groups, such as women with recurrent infections and children, while showing little benefit in elderly adults or people with bladder-emptying problems. Cranberry is used for prevention rather than to treat an active infection.
